scope.flow: injectSweepAndCall direct external call on TrailsRouter
scope.environment: TrailsRouter contract intended for delegatecall from smart wallet/shim

statements.text: injectSweepAndCall is a normal external function without an onlyDelegatecall or equivalent restriction, so it can execute directly on the router contract.
When called directly on the router, the function transfers tokens from msg.sender into address(this) (the router) and uses the router's own balance via _getSelfBalance/address(this).
The function is intended to run only via delegatecall from a smart wallet or shim, where address(this) and _getSelfBalance refer to the user's wallet, not the router.
Users may send funds to the router expecting stateless routing behavior.
The target is misconfigured, malicious, or fails.
injectSweepAndCall should only execute in a delegatecall context where address(this) is the user's wallet/shim, not directly on the router.
The router should remain stateless with no long-term funds; user balances should belong to the calling wallet.
The router accumulates and controls user funds, turning a stateless routing component into a stateful asset custodian.
If the target is misconfigured, malicious, or fails, funds remain in the router without a clear path to recovery.
Due to the previously reported missing delegatecall guard, an attacker can withdraw tokens from the router and drain these accumulated balances.

ambiguities: No concrete transaction or actor is shown executing the direct call; the trigger is described conditionally.
The report does not state whether the attacker is the same as the calling user or an unrelated party.
The prior injectAndCall bug enabling draining is referenced but not detailed here.
No specific amounts, tokens, or numeric bounds are given for the funds at risk.
